bounded_statement: The selected result's significance claim (18 of 24 records exceeding the 0.100 mg/L target, exact two-sided binomial p = 0.0227, declared distinguishable from the 0.5 benchmark at the 5% level) is not supported at the level of the declared independent unit. The 24 rows are three repeated storm samples from each of only 8 independent bioretention cells, and the binomial test treats each row as an independent Bernoulli trial. The data show near-total within-cell dependence: every cell is either 3/3 exceedances or 0/3, so the effective number of independent exceedance outcomes is 8, not 24. An exact two-sided binomial test on the 8 independent cells (6 of 8 exceeding) gives p ≈ 0.289, which does not reject the 0.5 benchmark at the 5% level. The record-level p-value of 0.0227 therefore overstates the evidence, and the report's significance conclusion does not survive analysis at the independent-unit level.

counterevidence_considered.description: The report is transparent about its unit of analysis: it explicitly frames the null hypothesis at the record level ('a record exceeds the target with probability 0.5') and discloses both the cell count (8) and the record count (24), so one could argue the claim is a deliberately record-level statement rather than a hidden inflation. This does not rescue the inference, because scipy.stats.binomtest still requires the 24 trials to be independent, and the data description plus the all-or-nothing per-cell pattern show they are not; but the disclosure means the mismatch is visible rather than concealed.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: Report discloses 8 cells, 3 storms, 24 records and states the null at the record level

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to defeat the pseudoreplication finding in three ways. (1) I checked whether rows might genuinely be independent despite the shared cell_id: the data description states each cell is a fixed structure sampled in all three storms, and the observed data show every cell is either 3/3 or 0/3 exceedances (perfect within-cell concordance), so the independence assumption of the row-level binomial test is empirically violated, not just formally. (2) I checked whether the conclusion is robust to the correction by recomputing the test at the independent-unit level: 6 of 8 cells exceed in every storm; the exact two-sided binomial probability for 6/8 under p=0.5 is 2 x (28+8+1)/256 ≈ 0.289, which does not reach the 5% level, so the significance claim does not survive. I also verified the reported record-level p-value (2 x 190051/16777216 ≈ 0.0227) to confirm the workflow did what the report says. (3) I considered whether the selected result could be read as purely descriptive (a share of 0.75 above target), in which case no independence assumption would be needed; but the selected result and the Result section explicitly invoke the binomial p-value and a 5%-level significance judgment, which is an inferential claim that depends on the invalid independent-trials assumption. All three attempts failed to overturn the finding.

root_cause: The workflow feeds all 24 rows of data/input.csv into scipy.stats.binomtest as 24 independent trials (n_exceed out of n_records), even though the data description identifies cell_id as the independent-unit column and states that the same eight cells reappear across the three storms. Each of the 8 authorized independent units (cells) enters the row-independent binomial procedure three times, once per storm, inflating the trial count from 8 to 24. Because within-cell exceedance outcomes are perfectly concordant in this dataset, the repeated entries carry almost no new information but triple the nominal sample size, shrinking the p-value from a non-significant ~0.289 (cell level) to the reported 0.0227 (record level).
